text:
- Anthropic's internal measures of AI R&D acceleration are partially published; several show acceleration, and internal automation of AI R&D is increasing. METR independently assessed this.
- Claude Mythos 5.2 is judged not to cross the RSP threshold: it does not double overall internal AI R&D progress versus an unassisted counterfactual. Acceleration estimates are uncertain.
- Task-based automated evaluations weren't run, since recent models exceed top human baselines.
- Weaknesses: it quit without running experiments in 63% of open-ended research sessions (medium effort), and left requested coding work undone in 6–13% of sessions (Fable 5.1: 4%).
- Users reported overconfident claims, weak research judgment, and early stopping; changed prompting and scaffolding seemed to reduce the early stopping.
- CoBench results are omitted pending evaluation fixes; Anthropic treats the weaknesses as limits on autonomy, not a capability ceiling.
